newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian govt offers aid for BHP steel shut-down.
newsitem.headline: Australian govt offers aid for BHP steel shut-down.

text.p: The Australian government said on Tuesday it would help the Hunter Valley region adjust to the planned shut-down of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's (BHP) steel works at Newcastle.

Prime Minister John Howard said he would talk to New South Wales (NSW) premier Bob Carr about setting up a joint national and state committee to examine alternative job strategies and projects to sustain economic development in the area.

"We will be committing resources equal to those promised by the NSW government (around A$10 million) but in a manner that is likely to be better targeted and more effectively spent," Howard said in a statement.
Howard and several of his ministers would be visiting the Hunter region shortly to assess economic and employment prospects and talk to the people of the region.
Other initiatives canvassed included fast-tracking major investment proposals in the area and offering employment advice to workers affected by the BHP closure, he said.
BHP announced at the end of April a wide-ranging restructure of its steel division, including the closure of its Newcastle steel-making operations and the laying off of 2,500 workers.
Based on a review of domestic and international steel operations, BHP said it would disband its international steel division and restructure BHP steel around four divisions.
It would phase-out steel making at its major Newcastle plant, north of Sydney, by the end of 1999 and also close its Geelong rod mill, in Victoria, and Sydney wire mill in 1999.
Newcastle's rod and bar mills would be retained and developed into the centre for BHP's rod, bar and wire business.
